text:
The Nifty 50 closed at 23,053.1, up 0.51% for the day and 2.0% over the past five sessions, while the broader Nifty 500 slipped 0.21% despite a 2.19% five‑day gain. Advances outnumbered declines by a wide margin (401 advances vs 92 declines), giving the market a “weak” breadth score of 28.9 but showing that the rally is still concentrated in a few stocks. Bank Nifty fell 0.41% to 54,686.95, indicating pressure on financials even as the overall index rose.

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) added a net ₹3,114.68 crore today, extending a four‑day buying streak, while Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) sold ₹392.2 crore, marking a two‑day net outflow. The options market shows a put‑call ratio (PCR) of 1.67 for Nifty, suggesting more put interest, with the “max‑pain” level around 23,250 and a call wall at 24,000. Bank Nifty’s PCR is near parity (0.96), and its max‑pain sits at 55,500, indicating balanced sentiment. Leading sectors were IT, pharma, healthcare and PSU banks, whereas media, private banks and broader financial services were weakening.

Watch the 23,032.77 support (S1) and 23,025.43 pivot on Nifty; a break below could test the 22,932.77 level, while a move above 23,145.77 (R1) may open the path toward the 23,400‑23,600 range highlighted in recent headlines. For Bank Nifty, the key levels are 54,488.97 (S1) and 54,778.73 (pivot). Keep an eye on global cues – especially US tech earnings and oil price moves – as they continue to influence Indian market direction.
